title: Sunraycer Renewables Closes $901M Financing for 479.5 MW Solar + 473 MWh BESS in Texas
detail: Sunraycer Renewables closed a $901 million project financing package with MUFG Bank, Ally Bank, Nomura Securities International, Nord/LB, and Societe Generale to build 479.5 MW of solar generation paired with 236.5 MW (473 MWh) of battery energy storage systems (BESS) across three Texas projects: Eagle Springs, Lupinus 1, and Lupinus 2. Construction on all three began in late 2025, with Eagle Springs expected to come online in late 2026. The deal represents Sunraycer's second portfolio financing in 12 months, bringing total capital raised to approximately $1.6 billion. Texas leads the US in utility-scale solar additions, and integrated solar-plus-storage projects are the fastest-growing segment of new US power capacity as grid operators prioritize dispatchable clean energy.

title: EDF-Abraxas JV Files EIS for 3+ GW Wind-to-Green Hydrogen Project in Newfoundland, Canada
detail: Exploits Valley Renewable Energy Corporation (EVREC), a joint venture of EDF and Abraxas, filed its Environmental Impact Statement for a 3+ GW onshore wind-to-green hydrogen and ammonia project in Central Newfoundland — one of Canada's largest renewable energy initiatives. At full capacity, the project targets 180,000 tonnes per year of renewable fuel-of-non-biological origin (RFNBO) hydrogen or up to 1 million tonnes per year of RFNBO ammonia for export. The EIS was filed under Newfoundland and Labrador provincial environmental assessment guidelines. The project represents a major step in Canada's green hydrogen export ambitions, leveraging Newfoundland's world-class wind resources to produce low-carbon hydrogen for European and Asian markets seeking to decarbonize heavy industry.

media.caption: EVREC files EIS for 3+ GW wind-to-green hydrogen project in Central Newfoundland — one of Canada's largest clean energy projects
